trial_court: Additional Sessions Court, Kozhikode, Crl.A No.89 of 2017
case_name: Kalathil Hamsakoya vs Rajashekar Palakkavu Kalam And Another

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kalathil Hamsakoya, aged 67 years, s/o Kaidaoyil Hasan Haji
parties.respondent_defendant: Rajashekar Palakkavu Kalam, aged 56 years, s/o E.Sekharakidavu, and State of Kerala

facts_of_case: Complainant alleged that Ext.P3 cheque for ₹39 lakhs dated 15.1.2013 issued by the accused was returned dishonoured due to insufficient funds and the accused failed to pay the amount covered by the cheque, thereby committing an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to explain how his signed cheque reached the hands of the complainant.
legal_principles.held: Accordingly, the accused has no explanation as to how his signed cheque reached at the hands of the complainant.

legal_principles.principle: A cheque is dishonoured if it is returned due to insufficient funds in the account of the drawer.
legal_principles.held: Ext.P4 memo would show that Ext.P3 cheque was dishonoured due to insufficient funds in the account of the accused.

outcome.final_order: The concurrent verdict of conviction and order of sentence against the revision petitioner was upheld.

keywords: Latin maxim: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea

prosecuting a case under Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
